solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a match gives you a light, as in 'have you got a light?'

explanation.surface: A slow bowler with a fine game is described as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinner is a slow bowler, which is the picture the surface paints; here it is just a spinning toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of the highest class or rank is excellent; the hyphenated adjective comes from the top division of a league.

parts.note: off means away, as in 'he's off today'

explanation.surface: A wave rises while time passes elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Swell looks like a wave or a verb, but here it is the noun for a fashionable person.
explanation.definitionFit: A toff is a posh, upper-class person, the same as the old slang noun a swell.

definitions.meaning: a game like blackjack, scoring to twenty-one
a temporary floating crossing supported on boats or floats

explanation.surface: A card game is named after a kind of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The card game sense is British usage for blackjack or twenty-one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the British card game twenty-one and a bridge laid on floating supports.

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A stage direction: exit stage left, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage left' reads as theatre jargon, but the clue splits after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg is one stage of a journey, race or tour, as in the final leg.

clue.text: Article supporting move over East German writer

indicators.note: in a down entry over means placed above, so the move word sits on top of East
in a down entry supporting means placed below, so the article sits beneath the rest

parts.note: to go is to move
E is the compass abbreviation for East
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A news article backs a move by an East German author.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, author of Faust, is Germany's most celebrated writer.

definitions.meaning: to fill with overwhelming joy, as in being carried away

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to carry from place to place and to send someone into raptures.

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word for note is taken away

parts.note: to note something is to mark it

explanation.surface: A ship of some renown sets sail.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's ark is the most famous vessel, a large boat built to survive the flood.

indicators.note: housing means holding within, so the word for locality surrounds the N

parts.note: an area is a locality or district

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood is home to a stadium in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a large enclosed venue for sport or shows, much like a stadium.

clue.text: Grasshopper in bottom of net caught by a kiddy playing

indicators.note: caught by means held within, so the rearranged letters surround the last letter of net
playing suggests the letters romping about into a new order
in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A child at play catches a grasshopper in the bottom of a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges AKIDDY into AKYDID, round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A katydid is a large green North American bush cricket, a kind of long-horned grasshopper.

indicators.note: the letter for good sits within the period of the closing act, so it goes inside that word

parts.note: the finale is the closing act of a show

explanation.surface: A performer pulls a trick in a show's closing act.
explanation.definitionFit: To finagle is to obtain something by trickery or sly manoeuvring, so it means to trick.

clue.text: Expert, extremely derisive in a gym

indicators.note: the outer letters of derisive are placed within A and PT

parts.note: PT, physical training, is what you do in school gym

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

explanation.surface: An expert sneers at the rest in a gymnasium.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adept is highly skilled, which is what an expert is; both serve as adjective or noun.

clue.text: He's out mostly working, save he's not the breadwinner

indicators.note: working suggests the letters being worked into a new order
most of the phrase is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to husband resources is to save or conserve them

explanation.surface: A man is away at work most of the time, except he doesn't earn the family's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the T from HESOUT, and 'working' rearranges HESOU into HOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who stays at home running the household while his partner earns the income fits the description exactly.

clue.text: Therefore spreading pâté's OK, in a way

parts.note: so means therefore, as in 'so I left'

indicators.note: spreading the letters out scatters them into a new order

explanation.surface: So putting pâté on toast is fine, in its own way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to signal that words are meant loosely or figuratively, just as 'in a way' does.

clue.text: Extremely small and quiet nursing home

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the word for quiet wraps round the word for home

parts.note: someone mute makes no sound, so is quiet
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A tiny, peaceful care home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing home' looks like one phrase, but 'nursing' is the containment signal and 'home' is IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, pronounced my-NEWT, is an adjective meaning tiny or extremely small.

clue.text: Cosmetic mother used to mask a blemish

indicators.note: to mask is to cover, so MA and A enclose the word for blemish

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a scar is a mark or blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: Mum uses make-up to hide a flaw on her face.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests concealer, but this make-up goes on the eyelashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is an eye make-up applied to darken and thicken eyelashes, a cosmetic.

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the fine-and-offer letters surround the gold

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a bid is an offer at auction
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a good bid that includes gold.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbid something is to refuse permission for it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Coffee shop worker and I sat in relaxed manner propping up counter

indicators.note: in a down entry propping up means placed underneath, so the rearranged letters go below the counter word

parts.note: a bar is a serving counter

indicators.note: a relaxed manner is loose, so the letters slip into a new order

explanation.surface: A café worker and I lounged at the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in relaxed manner' rearranges ISAT into ISTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista is someone who makes and serves espresso drinks in a café.

clue.text: Loss of silver accepted by lady

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so the lady word surrounds the silver

parts.note: a dame is a lady, a titled woman
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A woman takes in a quantity of lost silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage is harm or loss suffered, as in damage to a reputation or property.

clue.text: Competent head of security is locking up at mill

indicators.note: locking up means enclosing, so S and IS hold the word at between them
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill

explanation.surface: A capable security chief is shutting things up at the mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Something satisfactory is adequate or acceptable, which is what competent work is.

clue.text: Hard, however, when first husband lost

indicators.note: lost means that letter is removed from the word for however

parts.note: though means however, as in 'it's late, though'

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word husband

explanation.surface: Life is hard, though it was easier once the first husband had gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough and hard are synonyms, whether of a difficult task or a resistant material.

definitions.meaning: to support is to endorse or stand behind
the hind part of something, its far end

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning endorse and as a noun for the rear part of anything.

parts.note: something clipped has been cut

explanation.surface: Someone speaks with a crisp, clipped English way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a way of speaking; the definition is the written mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The acute is a diacritical mark, as in café, one kind of accent placed over a letter.

clue.text: Names I confused after onset of alarming medical condition

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the first letter of alarming
the onset of a word is its first letter
confused letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting names muddled is the start of a worrying illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia, loss of memory, is a recognised clinical disorder; mixing up names fits it neatly.

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the letters are read from bottom to top
cut means its last letter is cut off

parts.note: tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: A recipe: chop the fish, then make a fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the A from TUNA, and 'up' turns TUN round. Fruitcake looks like the bake; it is slang for a mad person.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut is slang for a crazy person, just as a fruitcake is in informal English.

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words Chelsea showground

explanation.surface: A tree stands on the Chelsea Flower Show grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chelsea Flower Show is a famous London garden show.
explanation.definitionFit: The ash is a common deciduous tree of the olive family.

parts.note: the keep is the strongest central tower of a castle
a track is a rough path

explanation.surface: Walk along part of a castle's footpath.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep track of something is to follow its progress or monitor it.
